    "contract_id": "qubo-ising-v0",
    "computational_intent_id": "exact-partial-pivot-selection",
    "migration_family": "combinatorial_optimization",
    "formulation": "Conditionally represent one activation of the pivot-selection expression as a one-hot QUBO over the eligible row indices col through n-1. The objective would have to select exactly the first index attaining the greatest Python abs(rows[i][col]) value. Any magnitude score, index tie-break term, and one-hot penalty must be proved to preserve that lexicographic result for every reachable state. Only line 13 is in scope; singularity checking, row swapping, elimination, back substitution, residual diagnostics, and report construction remain classical.",
    "input_encoding": "Encode n, col, and the current augmented-column values after all preceding swaps and elimination updates. One binary variable denotes each eligible row. A complete encoding must reproduce Python binary64 absolute-value and max behavior, including equal magnitudes, signed zero, and any nonfinite intermediate values reachable from finite inputs. Required coefficient precision, dynamic range, reversible or Hamiltonian-compatible data access, ancillary storage, and a sufficient one-hot penalty are unresolved.",
    "quantum_algorithm_family": "QUBO/Ising with a possible QAOA-style executor",
    "output_decoding": "Decode a one-hot row index and verify it against the original Python selection rule using the current row state. The quantum result may be used only if exact equivalence, including first-index tie behavior, is established. Invalid, infeasible, suboptimal, ambiguous, or uncertified samples cannot replace line 13. A semantics-preserving treatment of all unsupported states and failures remains an implementation obligation; merely declaring a classical fallback does not prove preservation.",
    "assumptions": [
      "The solve branch is active, n is positive, and the current column iteration has at least one eligible row.",
      "The dynamically modified augmented rows can be encoded without changing Python comparison behavior.",
      "The hybrid boundary preserves the serial dependence between each pivot selection and the elimination updates that determine later pivot values.",
      "Exact classical verification and any fallback costs are included in end-to-end resource and performance accounting."
    ],
    "risks": [
      "QAOA-style execution does not guarantee the exact optimum required by deterministic partial pivoting.",
      "Exact binary64 ordering, first-index tie-breaking, and one-hot feasibility may require impractical coefficient precision and dynamic range.",
      "Reachable nonfinite intermediate values may not admit the proposed ordinary magnitude-ranking formulation while preserving Python max and exception behavior.",
      "Repeated state loading, QUBO construction, optimization, measurement, decoding, and verification can exceed the cost of the original linear scan.",
      "A different pivot changes subsequent floating-point operations and can alter rounding, singularity detection, overflow behavior, the returned solution, deltas, and residual diagnostics.",
      "Finite development checks cannot establish full-domain equivalence, whole-plan correctness, or successful quantum execution."
    ],
    "expected_resource_characteristics": {
      "logical_variables_per_activation": "n-col one-hot variables before ancillary, arithmetic, comparison, or embedding overhead",
      "coupling_structure": "The squared one-hot constraint generally creates dense pairwise couplings among eligible-row variables.",
      "activations": "Up to n serial activations in solve mode; none in inspect mode or for an empty system.",
      "precision": "Must distinguish every relevant reachable binary64 magnitude and enforce the exact first-index tie rule.",
      "overheads": "Dynamic state preparation, coefficient construction, embedding, parameter optimization, shots, decoding, exact verification, and failure handling are unquantified.",
      "advantage_evidence": "None supplied."
    },
    "rationale": "This is a conditional structural analysis, not a correctness or adoption claim. Migration remains contingent on a full-domain encoding and proof that exact classical semantics are preserved."
  },
  "rationale": "The finite pivot selection at kernel.py line 13 is the only localized region with a plausible supported-family formulation. It evaluates range(col, n) using the current augmented rows and chooses the greatest abs(rows[i][col]); because the range is ascending and Python max retains the first maximal item, lowest-index tie-breaking is part of the required semantics. Its dependencies are n, col, and rows as initialized at line 11 and mutated by earlier swaps and elimination at lines 16-20. It activates only when program.py lines 22-23 enter solve mode, n is nonzero, and the corresponding column iteration is reached. The boundary must preserve the exact-zero singularity check at lines 14-15, the swap at line 16, elimination at lines 17-20, back substitution at lines 21-25, and residual and report behavior in program.py lines 19-27. Structural eligibility is true only at the abstract formulation level: a finite one-hot selection objective can represent an argmax if an exact scoring and tie-breaking encoding exists. The supplied finite-check observation does not prove that such an encoding covers every reachable binary64 state, and neither excluded states nor a declared fallback count as verified repairs. Practical suitability is false because this is a small linear scan inside serial elimination, whereas a hybrid implementation would require repeated dynamic data encoding, exact optimization, verification, and strict exception preservation. Benchmark support is false because no workload, hardware, resource, quantum execution, or advantage evidence is supplied, and the program explicitly is not a compliant HPL performance run. The remaining elimination and residual code is dense numerical computation rather than a justified unstructured-search or combinatorial-optimization migration target.",
  "structural_eligibility": true,
  "practical_suitability": false,
  "benchmark_supported": false,
  "computational_intent": "For each elimination column, select the earliest eligible row whose current pivot has maximum absolute value while preserving Python binary64 behavior and all downstream solution, exception, and reporting semantics.",
  "assumptions": [
    "Only the supplied source, software contract, draft migration contracts, and limited observations are considered.",
    "No quantum memory, coherent data-loading mechanism, backend capability, workload distribution, or performance advantage is assumed.",
    "Exact Python pivot ordering and first-index tie-breaking are mandatory and cannot be weakened to approximate success.",
    "Validation, inspect mode, empty-system behavior, residual computation, named report construction, and nonmutation remain classical."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "A probabilistic, approximate, or incorrectly tie-broken pivot violates the software contract.",
    "Reachable exceptional floating-point states can make a simple numeric QUBO objective semantically incomplete.",
    "Objective construction and exact classical verification can perform work comparable to or greater than the original selection.",
    "Sequential elimination prevents independent batching because each selected pivot changes later candidate values.",
    "Finite checks provide neither full-domain equivalence nor evidence that the conditional quantum plan is executable.",
    "The HPL attribution supports the classical algorithm description, not quantum suitability or advantage."
  ],

No reversible oracle, coherent data-access construction, resource bound, or deterministic error policy is supplied, so applicability is unresolved."

This does not establish an implementable or correct migration: exact coefficient construction, penalty sufficiency, treatment of reachable nonfinite states, feasibility, backend precision, exact-optimum recovery, verification, and end-to-end resources remain unresolved obligations."
    }
  ]
